$comment: Scrapbook type direction. Fonts come from foundations/typography/source/pairings.json (rated in fit) or from newPairings below. Type in a scrapbook looks found: newspaper headlines, typewriter labels, printed tickets. Sizes are rules of thumb unless a source is given.
character: Found type, set with care: a bold, newspaper-like headline face cut into strips, a plain readable body on paper, and a typewriter mono for labels, tickets and dates. Mixed cut-out letters and handwriting are spices, used once, never the meal.

anatomy.$comment: What to look for when judging a typeface for this approach.

weight.why: Headlines are cut out and pasted onto busy backgrounds; heavy strokes survive overlap, rotation and texture.

width.why: Condensed headlines fit on narrow strips, like newspaper headlines.

texture.why: Type should look found in print (newspaper, label, typewriter), so the hand lives in the collage and the notes.

xHeight.why: Text sits at small sizes on labels and tickets and must stay readable when rotated.

mono.why: Labels, tickets, receipts and stamps are typewritten or printed in mono in real life.

avoid: Thin hairline serifs (break on textured or rotated strips)
Script and handwriting fonts for headlines or body
Ransom-note fonts that randomise every letter (unreadable, and the real thing is cut by hand)

fit.$comment: core = recommended, good = works, accent = special cases, avoid = not for this approach.

bricolage-figtree.why: Bricolage's heavy, irregular grotesque reads like a cut-out headline; Figtree keeps notes and body clear.

schibsted.why: Sturdy news grotesque (made for a newspaper group); heavy weights look clipped from print.

young-onest.why: The chunky soft serif suits journals and food; Onest stays readable on small labels.

plex.why: IBM Plex Mono is an excellent label and ticket face; the serif headline is a little formal for collage.

source.why: Very readable for text-heavy album pages; the serif headline needs the heavy weight to hold up.

fraunces-commissioner.why: Heavy Fraunces looks like vintage print for ransom letters and headlines; keep it to one weight.

instrument.why: Elegant condensed serif suits a fashion or editorial cut-up; its thin strokes break on texture, so use it large and on clean paper only.

alegreya.why: Literary and calligraphic; works for a Victorian-album feel, less for punk or social collage.

nunito.why: Rounded terminals look like app UI, not found print; the collage turns childish.

newPairings.name: Cut and Paste
newPairings.mood: Newspaper headline cut into strips, with typewritten labels. Bold, plain and documentary; the default for this approach.
newPairings.bestFor: Scrapbook posters, social collage, zines, events, local businesses.

display.style: Grotesque with a width axis, from extra condensed to expanded
display.notes: Use widths 75-100 for headline strips; heavy weights survive rotation and overlap.

newPairings.name: Zine
newPairings.mood: A tall, condensed poster headline in sentence case, a friendly grotesque for text, and a worn typewriter for labels. Loud but legible.
newPairings.bestFor: Music, events, campaigns, youth brands, flyers.

display.notes: Single weight; very tall x-height. Keep headlines to 2-3 strips. The mono, Special Elite (Astigmatic), is a worn typewriter face under the Apache License 2.0 rather than OFL (still free for commercial use); labels and stamps only, never body text.

body.style: Grotesque, slightly wide, optimised for screen at text sizes

newPairings.name: Clippings
newPairings.mood: A heavy, high-contrast serif like a magazine headline, with a clean sans and a quiet mono. For softer, journal-like collage.
newPairings.bestFor: Lifestyle, food, travel, gifts, journaling products.

display.case: Sentence case; italic for one emphasised word
display.notes: Use at 28 px / 20 pt and above, on clean paper strips; hairlines are thin.

accents.$comment: Optional extra faces for one short handwritten note or marker label. They are accents outside the pairing, used under the limits below. The guide's general rule is no handwriting fonts; this approach allows one note because the hand-written note is part of the medium. Hand-lettering a note is better still.

fonts.use: Marker label on kraft or tape.

limits.minSize: Body size x 1.2 (handwriting reads smaller than type at the same size)
never: anything a reader must read to act

ransomNote.$comment: Cut-out mixed letters, after punk and Dada collage.
ransomNote.tileRule: Each letter on its own cut tile (paper, ink, support or accent); tile rotation -7 to +7 degrees; gap 2-4 units.
ransomNote.faces: Take the 3 faces from the product's pairing (display, body, mono), plus at most one accent tile in a different weight. Do not load extra fonts for ransom letters.
ransomNote.contrast: Every tile must pass 4.5:1 between letter and tile (ink on paper or yellow, paper on ink or a dark accent).
never: brand names (unless the brand already does it)
words that read as a threat

typeWithArt.onPaper: All text sits on paper: a torn strip, a label, a note, a ticket. Never set text directly on photos or busy collage.
typeWithArt.stripPadding: Strip extends 0.25-0.4 em past the text on each side and 0.15 em above and below the cap height and descenders.
typeWithArt.weightMatch: Headline stem close to the hand-mark line (about 1.4% of the artboard's short side) or heavier.
typeWithArt.alignment: Each strip left-aligned to a shared edge; rotations vary per strip within -2 to +2 degrees, so the edge still reads as one.
typeWithArt.spacing: Strips may overlap each other by up to 10% of their height, never the letters.

sizes.$comment: Headline cap height as a share of the canvas height, and body text minimums. Rules of thumb. Scrapbook headlines are a little smaller than minimal styles because the strips add visual weight.
sizes.viewingDistance: Sign-industry rule of thumb: about 1 inch (25 mm) of letter height for every 10 feet (3 m) of viewing distance for basic legibility; double it for comfortable reading.

measure.source: Bringhurst, The Elements of Typographic Style (45-75 for body); shorter here because text sits on small paper pieces (rule of thumb).

setting.case: Sentence case everywhere. Capitals only for labels of one to three words (ADMIT ONE, a stamp ring).
setting.fontsPerPiece: The pairing's 2-3 faces, plus at most one accent face for one note.
setting.rag: Ragged right; one strip per headline line; no justified text.
setting.numbers: Use the mono for dates, times, prices, ticket numbers and codes.

rules: Found type, set with care: heavy headline strips, readable body on paper, typewriter mono for facts.
Every piece of text sits on paper.
Ransom-note letters on one headline word at most.
One handwritten note of six words or fewer, never the headline, body or call to action.
Three sizes, two weights, sentence case, left-aligned.
